clauses.reason: The sole operative sentence of Executive Order 8341 revokes Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940, which abolished Customs Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee) and made related changes to customs ports and districts; its operative words are 'is hereby revoked'. A present-tense revocation with no later effective date is carried out when the order takes effect, so the command was exhausted by performance on the order's signing date, 1940-02-08, which is recorded as the end. The filing date February 9, 1940 and the issue date February 10, 1940 are the alternatives if effectiveness is dated from filing or publication. The Federal Register docket line reads 'Filed, February 9, 1940;' and the issue is headed 'Washington, Saturday, February 10, 1940'.

research_rationale:
Identity and text: the held original is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register issue (5 FR 643, PDF pages 1-1, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-1940-02-10/pdf/FR-1940-02-10.pdf, sha256 7f27ace7dd1e7d0878cc9fedf7b7984f89e101ceaf1db38ac106f6d598061159); the text layer is OCR, the page image is not held in the repository, and the order was identified from the text layer. The order's heading, subject, signature date and closing number tag appear together as one short order whose whole text is the clause. Inventory: one operative sentence revoking Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940, which abolished Customs Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee) and made related changes to customs ports and districts; there is no other clause. End: a present-tense revocation is carried out when the order takes effect, and the order postpones nothing, so the command was exhausted by performance on its signing date 1940-02-08; the filing date February 9, 1940 and the issue date February 10, 1940 are the alternative dates if effectiveness is dated from filing or publication. Later instruments: the packet's later-events search of Office of the Federal Register disposition notes (1937 onward) and its current-law searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR were selected after reading their coverage notes, and each returned no hit for this order. A later revocation or repeal of the order is not needed to end a command that was already performed.

savings.reason: The held text contains no savings or transition clause. Its single command, revocation of Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940, which abolished Customs Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee) and made related changes to customs ports and districts, was completed when the order took effect. The revoked order's loss of effect is a completed consequence that survives as an accrued result, not as a continuing command of this order.
